content.summary: The complete two-star-to-terminal chain retains the correct hypotheses. The degree≤19 requirement of the internal incidence application is discharged using the inherited unconditional high-point ceiling. Literal Profile B then contradicts the eighty bound, and only the global assembly requires I27 via Profile A and the inherited boundary reduction. No hidden support restriction or claim migration was found.

checks.scope: Integrated two-star theorem and terminal dependency chain
checks.method: Trace frozen TwoHighEighty.lean through TwoStarBridge.residual_degree_bounds and TwoHighIncidence, inspect the inherited high_points_card_le_two declaration in Erdos20V12HighCardTwo.lean, and compare with manuscript Sections1–3 and the previously inspected terminal assembly.
checks.observation: The public two-star root derives exactly two high points from the distinct degree20 centers and the unconditional high-point cap. The rank-four point cap then excludes degree20 for every other point, giving degree≤19. The residual bridge excludes both centers from U and deducts five star incidences, or ten on U∩V, to obtain14 and9. The general incidence theorem needs no sunflower or support-size premise; specializing |U|=12 gives residual≤40, and the disjoint-star partition gives total≤80. Literal B supplies exactly two high points and the per-member high cap, so B is excluded independently of I27. FinalEighty uses that exclusion and the I27-conditional A exclusion to obtain the stated conditional global result.

checks.method: Verify unchanged manuscript bytes against the current snapshot and compare abstract, Theorems1–3, Corollary4, formal-scope paragraph and revised Section6 against the dependency chain.
checks.observation: Only the two-star structural result is called unconditional locally. The external ordinary corollary remains distinct from the local I27→G80 theorem; the support53 reductions and universal45 diagnostics do not enter the chain. The initial profile classification is invoked under I27, not used to prove the unrestricted two-star theorem.
